note: Preview P6 budgets (issue #170, docs/design/reference-equantic-ui.md section 7.4; ADR-045 consequences), completed by issue #395. Checked by scripts/check_preview_budget.py. TWO-SIDED RATCHET: an entry fails when it is worse than its budget by more than tolerance.worse, AND when it is better by more than tolerance.better (the budget went stale and must be tightened with --update, which never loosens any entry). The two sides carry different percentages on purpose: a single symmetric band wide enough for a noisy timing row would make the lower bound negative and silently disable the staleness side, so 'better' stays under 100% for every entry. ALL THREE ENTRIES ARE NOW ENFORCED. download_gzip_bytes is exactly reproducible for a fixed input and zlib build, so its 5%/1% band is measurement slack, not noise cover. THE TWO LATENCY ROWS ARE NO LONGER RAW WALL CLOCK (issue #395): each probe process times a fixed integer workload and the row is measured_ms * measurement.calibration_reference_ms / calibration_ms, so the runner's speed cancels and the pin means 'this much time on the recorded reference profile'. Evidence for the change: the eight Pages runs of 2026-11-16/17 measured cold_engine_ready_ms between 16.552 and 28.272 ms and edit_compile_ms between 0.083 and 0.223 ms with no relevant source change -- 1.7x and 2.7x of runner noise, which no honest band could both cover and detect a regression through. The same rows were then measured on one box over 15 fresh processes: raw spread 1.06x idle and 1.08x with twelve CPU-burner processes on twelve threads, normalized spread 1.04x in both cases. WHAT THAT DOES NOT PROVE, so a reviewer can disagree: it assumes the ratio of integer-arithmetic speed to Wasm-compile speed is roughly constant across x86-64 runner generations. Only one host was measured. Both sides of the latency band are wide for that unmeasured component (worse 100%, better 50%, against 5%/1% for the deterministic size row), and every run also prints cold_engine_ready_raw_ms/edit_compile_raw_ms plus calibration_ms so a human can tell 'the code got slower' from 'the runner class changed'. If a later lane shows the ratio is not stable across hosts, the honest fix is to demote these two rows to warn and ratchet a work counter instead; the ratchet code does not change, so that is a status edit plus this note. THE DOWNLOAD BUDGET NOW COVERS EVERY MODULE THE STUDIO LOADS (issue #395). It used to weigh tessera_diagnostics only; the studio lazy-loads three modules (ADR-054 decision 3) and the two it did not weigh are the larger ones. It is still ONE entry on the total, so one regression fails once rather than three times, and every module's own gzip size rides in `recorded` so a report names the file that grew. The two latency rows remain the ENGINE'S SHARE ONLY: cold time-to-first-frame also needs the browser's HTML/CSS parse and a WebGPU frame (P3, not landed), and edit-to-view needs that frame too; the browser lane adds cold_first_frame_ms/edit_to_view_ms beside them. HOW TO RE-RECORD (the mechanism, not a number): a TIGHTENING is `--update`, which writes a lower pin and refuses anything else. A RAISE is a reviewed edit of the pin in the diff with the reason recorded here -- --update refuses it by design, because a re-pin on a loaded box would record machine load as headroom. To re-record, run `python -B scripts/check_preview_budget.py --check --size-only --module-dir <built module dir>` for the size rows (fully deterministic: the number must match to the byte or the encoder changed) and `python -B scripts/check_preview_budget.py --check --module-dir <dir> --node $EMSDK_NODE` for the latency rows (write down the raw and normalized values, and whether calibration_ms was near calibration_reference_ms). Changing measurement.calibration_reference_ms rebases every latency pin at once: do that only with the same reviewed-edit treatment as encoder.

source.modules: tessera_diagnostics_wasm, tessera_scene_preview_wasm and tessera_canvas_wasm (src/compiler/codegen/CMakeLists.txt), the three browser modules ADR-054 decision 3 lazy-loads. Each module's two files (the .js loader and the .wasm) are measured from the module directory, not from dist/: they are linked engine artifacts the Pages lane copies next to the page, never bundled. All three are weighed because the studio loads all three -- diagnostics for the default view, scene preview for the Scene tab, canvas for the Canvas tab -- and until issue #395 only diagnostics was (the smallest of the three).
source.page: the built page, designer/web/dist/ (issue #422, ADR-054 decision 6). The measurement walks that directory rather than naming files: Vite emits content-hashed assets (assets/index-<hash>.js, assets/index-<hash>.css) that a fixed list cannot name, and walking the directory keeps the rule the old PAGE_FILES list existed for -- an asset that ships is an asset that is weighed -- true by construction. The tree is index.html (the mount point), the hashed JS and CSS chunks (React 19 chrome plus the three view sessions), the two pre-merge redirect stubs, redirect.js, samples.json and the IBM Plex Sans subset plus its license (issue #387), which Vite copies from designer/web/public/. The three Wasm loaders are not in the bundle: they are lazy import()s the Pages lane copies next to the page, and they are weighed from the module directory instead.
source.runtime: the modules run in the Emscripten Node host ($EMSDK_NODE in CI); a browser host cannot be measured in this lane

download_gzip_bytes.measures: gzip-9 bytes of the whole designer/web/ page directory plus all six files of the three modules the studio loads (tessera_diagnostics, tessera_scene_preview, tessera_canvas: the .js loader and the .wasm payload of each); the transfer a browser pays once every view has been opened

cold_engine_ready_ms.measures: calibration-normalized minimum over 5 fresh processes of (module instantiation + first compile): the ENGINE's share of cold time-to-first-frame, NOT the frame. Normalized as measured_ms * 15.69 / calibration_ms, so the runner's speed cancels; the raw figure is printed on every run as cold_engine_ready_raw_ms

edit_compile_ms.measures: calibration-normalized minimum over 5 fresh processes of the per-edit minimum compile of 30 edits after 5 warm-up compiles: the ENGINE's share of edit-to-view, NOT the frame. Normalized as measured_ms * 15.69 / calibration_ms; the raw figure is printed on every run as edit_compile_raw_ms
